findings.reason: a builder who trusts "both also recognise the head suffix" may not extend the two readers, and the claim must instead state that they are extended to strip the suffix.
findings.text: §3 states "Both also recognise the head suffix, so a later round still resolves to the run it reviewed", but neither `_task_identity`/`_reviewed_run_id` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:436`) nor `_resolved_reviewed_run_id` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:65`) strips a trailing `-<head[:12]>`: called with the later-round id §3 proposes they each return `structural-guards-have-one-home-71bb011d8abc` rather than the reviewed run's id, so §3's fourth case ("resolve every round's id to the reviewed run") cannot pass on the tree as it stands

findings.reason: the shared rule must be applied where the id is actually composed (or the printed `next_action` command composed by `_review_dispatch_action` at `recovery_review_subject.py:844` would still carry the reused id and collide on a hand run), so `recovery_review_subject.py` belongs in §3's write paths.
findings.text: §3 declares the reused id is repaired "In `dispatch_review_for_run`" and lists its write paths as `recovery_review_dispatch.py`, `repair.py`, the two id readers and the new test, but the run-review node id is composed at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:652` (`"node_id": f"{REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX}{source_node}"`), and that file is not a write path — §3 names only the plan-review and code-review id sites there as "outside this section"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every href resolves once extensionless targets are read as `<path>.html` (`/reckon/plans/the-review-loop-runs-without-hand-steps`, `/reckon/plans/a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk`, and the evidence anchor `/reckon/evidence/archive/a-moved-head-is-reviewed-landed.html#s2-why-the-reflex-launched-nothing`, which exists at that file's `id="s2-why-the-reflex-launched-nothing"`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §3's four cases is a measurable outcome (one review keyed to B, a carried-forward review, no launch, distinct third-round id) and §3 declares and executes a negative control (the reused round id restored must fail the runtime-source resume case).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3's negative control is logged under the run directory, a durable crew path outside any session scratchpad or node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §3 carries no plan label, ticket number or version tag into a symbol; the test file is named for the mechanism (`tests/test_a_resumed_head_is_reviewed.py`), not for this plan's slug.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3 asserts both id readers already recognise the head suffix, and it places the node-id composition "in `dispatch_review_for_run`" although the review node id is composed once, in `_review_dispatch_fields` at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:652`, a file §3 does not list among its write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable: give a re-review round a node identity and worktree path distinct from the round before.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan's `informs` relationship (`a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk`) resolves, and §3's cross-plan citations (`the-review-loop-runs-without-hand-steps` §3, merge `7c923144a`) name a landed commit, so no dependency §3 needs is missing.
